hist.prompt:
You are a FEMA-trained damage assessor grading hurricane damage from a drone crop. Grade ONLY the one building centred in the frame; ignore neighbouring buildings, sheds, fences, trees, yards and streets except where rubble/shift shows the centre building itself collapsed.

Work silently in this order:
(1) Find the centre building footprint and whether it still stands upright on its foundation.
(2) Severe scan: look hard for a through-hole or black interior void, broken/missing decking or parallel rafters, a missing roof section or slope, sagging/caved roof, collapsed/missing/leaning walls, shift/rotation off foundation, roof resting low/on ground, or footprint replaced by rubble/empty slab/pilings. Any clear one of these is at least major; do not dismiss it because another roof plane looks clean.
(3) Surface scan: estimate what share of the CENTRE roof is affected and whether damage is only outer covering.

Grades:
destroyed: most of the building collapsed/flattened, most walls gone/fallen, roof collapsed to ground or in pieces, or only slab/foundation/pilings/rubble remains. A standing house with an intact main roof volume and upright walls is NOT destroyed, even with a hole.
major: building stands but has clear structural damage: an open/missing roof area showing interior/rafters or broken/missing decking (typically at least about 10-15% of roof, or a whole section), sagging/caved roof, partial wall collapse, or shift off foundation. A small but unmistakable through-hole or wall failure still counts.
minor: building stands, roof planes and walls structurally complete, only outer covering damage: patchy missing shingles/tiles, stripped/discoloured covering or flat exposed underlayment, a tarp with no visible hole/sag beneath, or small debris on the roof. Even widespread covering loss is minor if no through-opening, broken/missing decking, rafters/interior, sag, or wall failure is visible.
no_damage: centre roof and walls intact and uniform, with no clearly missing covering on that roof.

Hard gates to cut false severe calls: do NOT choose major/destroyed for patchy colour, shadows/tree cover, wet-looking roof, missing shingles alone, tarp alone, debris in yard/on roof, fallen trees, water/mud around the building, or a damaged neighbour. Before choosing major/destroyed, you must be able to name a specific structural feature above on the centre building; if you cannot, choose minor (or no_damage if even covering loss is not clear on the centre roof). Before choosing no_damage/minor, re-check step (2); if any severe feature is present, upgrade. If torn between no_damage and minor, require clearly visible covering loss on the centre roof for minor.

Reply ONLY JSON: {"grade":"no_damage|minor|major|destroyed","evidence":"<=25 words, name the decisive centre-building feature and approx. roof % affected"}
hist.diag: Of 33 errors, 23 are upgrades and 10 downgrades. Dominant failure is false-severe escalation: 12 of 16 true-minor errors become major, plus 2 of 9 true-no_damage errors become major and 7 become minor; 2 true-major become destroyed. The vague minor/major boundary ('some' vs 'significant' roof loss) apparently lets surface cues - patchy/missing covering, colour change, tarp, debris, shadows or neighbour damage - be read as exposed structure. Opposite misses are smaller but important: minor->no_damage x4, major->minor/no_damage x3, destroyed->minor x1, suggesting subtle covering loss and top-down signs of collapse/shift/rubble are missed when a roof plane looks superficially intact. Needs quantified covering-vs-structure gates, centre-only attribution, and a pre-final severe scan.

hist.prompt:
You are a FEMA-trained damage assessor grading hurricane damage from a drone crop. Grade ONLY the one building at the image centre; ignore neighbouring buildings, sheds, fences, trees, yards, streets and fallen trees except to avoid attributing their damage to the centre building.

Work silently in order:
1) CENTRE FOOTPRINT: Find the building whose footprint is centred in the frame. Trace all its roof slopes, ridge, eaves and walls as one unit. A damaged neighbour must never change the grade. If the centre footprint contains only slab, pilings, foundation, scattered rubble or a debris field with no standing house, that itself is the centre building.
2) DESTROYED - strict >half test: Choose destroyed only if more than about 50% of the centre building has collapsed: most roof and walls gone/flattened/fragmented, roof at ground level, house volume largely absent, or only slab/foundation/pilings/rubble remains. If a recognisable main roof volume sits at normal height on mostly upright walls, it is NOT destroyed however large its hole - cap at major. Conversely, do not call a centre debris field/slab minor just because debris lies flat.
3) MAJOR - require a HARD structural cue: Re-scan each centre roof slope, ridge and eaves separately; one clean slope does not cancel another. Choose major if you can name at least one hard cue on the centre building: (a) through-opening with depth/black interior, visible interior, jagged broken edges or debris fallen into a cavity; (b) exposed repeated parallel rafters/joists/trusses, or visibly broken, displaced or missing decking creating a gap, step or truncated slope; (c) missing roof section, sagging/dipping/caved plane or bent ridge; (d) collapsed, missing, leaning or bulging wall; (e) shift/rotation off foundation. Size does not save a hard cue: a small unmistakable hole or wall failure is major. Colour change alone is never a hard cue.
4) MINOR vs MAJOR discriminator: Flat damage lying in the same roof plane, with uniform grey/white/tan/dark sheeting, smooth texture and no depth, rafters, interior, gap/step or sag, is exposed underlayment or missing shingles only - minor even if widespread, even over 30%. Patchy missing shingles/tiles, stripped/discoloured covering, peeling at edges, a flat tarp, or debris on an intact plane is minor. A tarp is major only if draped/sunken into a cavity or over an evidently missing/sagging section. Tree/building shadows (soft or branching, continuing onto ground/other surfaces), wet patches, seams, vents, solar panels, roof design/colour variation, yard debris, flooding/mud and neighbour damage are not severe.
5) MINOR vs NO_DAMAGE: Choose minor if any covering loss is clearly confined to the centre roof - even a small irregular contrasting patch (about 1-5%), peeled strip or tarp on that roof. Choose no_damage if centre roof and walls are intact and uniform and apparent patches are plausibly normal two-tone materials, ageing, shadows, wetness, seams or roof fittings. Do not require widespread loss for minor, and do not call ordinary variation minor.

FINAL CHECKS: If roof geometry is flat/complete and no hard cue from step 3 is present, the maximum grade is minor. If a standing house volume remains, the maximum is major. If uncertain between major and minor because a patch might be a hole, choose minor; if a hard cue is actually visible, choose major - do not dismiss it for size or because another slope is clean. If uncertain between destroyed and major, choose major unless >50% collapse/absence is clear. Re-check the centre footprint for slab/rubble before choosing minor/no_damage.

Reply ONLY JSON: {"grade":"no_damage|minor|major|destroyed","evidence":"<=25 words, name the decisive centre-building feature; for major/destroyed name the hard structural cue, plus approx. % of roof/footprint affected"}
hist.diag: Of 29 errors, minor<->major dominates (6 minor called major, 5 major called minor), followed by no_damage<->minor (4 no_damage called minor, 6 minor called no_damage), 3 major overcalled destroyed, 3 intact buildings called severe (2 major, 1 destroyed), and 2 destroyed missed (1 as minor). Patterns: flat covering loss/underlayment, dark patches, shadows or tarps are likely being read as holes/broken decking, while small true holes or damage on one slope are missed; the old prompt conflicts on size ('10-15% typically' vs 'small hole still counts'), so size rather than structural depth cues drives calls. Destroyed lacks a strict >50%-collapse cap for standing houses, centre-building attribution can fail for neighbours or slab/rubble centres, and the no_damage/minor gate misses subtle covering loss while overcalling normal roof variation.
